page.text:
Two elements $x, y$ in a group *commute* when their product is
independent of order: $x * y = y * x$. In general groups—such as
permutation groups $S_n$ or matrix groups
$\operatorname{GL}_n$—multiplication is profoundly non-commutative. The
degree to which commutativity fails is measured by the *commutator*
$[x, y] = x * y * x^{-1} * y^{-1}$, which equals the identity $e$ if and
only if $x$ and $y$ commute.
